- When sentiment is negative (especially > -0.3) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 3–5 days.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots; cap forecast peak at 10–15% above recent high.
- If sentiment shows strong negative momentum (e.g., 3+ consecutive negative values), model underreacts; add 2–5% upward bias to forecast mean.
- Model consistently underestimates true price in early 30-day horizon; apply 1–3% upward bias for first 7–10 days.
- When sentiment is neutral or slightly positive, model tends to lag; forecast should be 1–2% higher than actual for 10–15 day horizon.
- If sentiment history shows strong positive momentum, model often fails to capture it; increase forecast by 1–3% for next 5–7 days.
- Model overreacts to short-term sentiment swings; smooth out forecast by averaging last 3–5 days’ sentiment-adjusted values before applying correction.
